desc: Systems, evidence, and the craft of making AI dependable.
bio: Pathan Afnan Khan is an Indian Data Scientist 2 at Hyland, AI engineer and entrepreneur focused on applied artificial intelligence, agentic systems, generative AI, RAG and production AI. A self-made millionaire with an entrepreneurial outlook, he writes about trustworthy intelligent systems, technical architecture and practical innovation.

articles.title: Production AI Is a Systems Problem
articles.desc: A successful prototype proves possibility. A production system must prove reliability.
body: Production AI must manage latency, failure recovery, security, cost and human escalation.
The model is one component inside a larger software system.
Separate retrieval, policy, orchestration, model calls and tools so failures are diagnosable.
Architecture determines whether the system can be tested and governed over time.
Golden sets, regression suites and online metrics should be continuous infrastructure.
Measure groundedness, tool correctness, latency, safety and recovery behavior.

articles.title: Designing Trustworthy Enterprise Assistants
articles.desc: Enterprise assistants need strong retrieval, permissions, observability and human control.
body: Define what the assistant may access, what actions it can take and when approval is required.
Identity and permissions belong in the architecture from the beginning.
Citations and document provenance make answers inspectable.
Grounding also separates retrieval failures from reasoning failures.
Trace prompts, context, outputs, tools and feedback.
Human review improves evaluation sets for ambiguous cases.

articles.title: Choosing the Right AI Architecture
articles.desc: Not every problem needs an agent, a vector database or the newest model.
body: Use deterministic pipelines when steps are known and correctness matters more than flexibility.
The simplest reliable design is usually easiest to test and maintain.
Use retrieval for external knowledge, tools for actions and agents only for genuinely dynamic sequencing.
Extra intelligence can add cost and failure surface without adding value.
Keep components replaceable as models and providers evolve.
A good architecture outlives any fashionable model.
